sections.h2: Where is Polk County, Oregon, and what is in it?
sections.html:
Polk County sits in western Oregon, west of Salem, with its eastern half in the Willamette Valley. It covers about 744 square miles, and the Willamette River forms its eastern border with Marion County.

The Oregon Provisional Legislature created the county on December 22, 1845, and named it for President James K. Polk. The county seat is Dallas, which took that name in 1852 after Vice President George M. Dallas. Other cities include Independence, Monmouth, Falls City and part of Willamina. West Salem, on the county's side of the river, is part of the City of Salem.

About two-thirds of the county, the western part, is forest. Laurel Mountain in that forested area is described as the wettest place in Oregon. For a seller, that means two very different kinds of property: valley lots near Salem and hill or timber parcels toward the Coast Range.

sections.h2: Polk County property tax facts from the Census Bureau
sections.html:
The Census Bureau puts Polk County at 90,037 people as of July 1, 2025, with 36,026 housing units. Owners occupy 64.7% of homes, and the median owner-occupied home was valued at $454,700 for 2020 to 2024.

MeasurePolk County
Population, July 1, 2025 estimate90,037
Housing units, July 1, 2025 estimate36,026
Owner-occupied housing rate, 2020 to 202464.7%
Median value of owner-occupied homes, 2020 to 2024$454,700
Median household income, 2020 to 2024$85,118
Persons per household, 2020 to 20242.65
Mean travel time to work, 2020 to 202425.3 minutes

A 25 minute average commute fits a county where many residents drive east to Salem for work. These are county-wide figures, so a farm outside Rickreall and a house in Monmouth can sit far from the median.

sections.h2: What drives the Polk County economy?
sections.html:
Agriculture, forest products, manufacturing and education are the main industries. Western Oregon University in Monmouth is a major employer, and the county has the second-largest wine grape acreage in Oregon.

Lumber shaped the county seat for decades. Dallas was the birthplace of Willamette Industries, founded there in 1906 as the Willamette Valley Lumber Company. Weyerhaeuser bought that company in 2002, and the Dallas mill closed in 2009. West Valley Hospital is the city's only hospital, and Chemeketa Community College runs a Polk Center campus there.

Nine K-12 school districts serve the county, and it falls within the Chemeketa Community College district. In Monmouth and Independence, the Central School District covers both cities, including Talmadge Middle School and Central High School.

sections.h2: How do Dallas, Monmouth, Independence and Falls City differ for homeowners?
sections.html:
Each city has a different size, setting and housing mix, which shows up in what sellers face. All four are in the Salem metropolitan area.

  • Dallas: The 2020 census counted 16,854 residents. It sits along Rickreall Creek, about 15 miles west of Salem. Annual precipitation averages about 47.8 inches, mostly in winter, with snow averaging about 4.9 inches.
  • Monmouth: Population was 11,110 in 2020, with a median age of 26.2, which reflects Western Oregon University. It lies about 12 miles west of Salem on Oregon Route 99W.
  • Independence: Population was 9,828 in 2020. It stands on the west bank of the Willamette River along Oregon Route 51, and a December 1861 flood wiped out its commercial district and farms.
  • Falls City: Population was 1,051 in 2020. It lies in the hills of the Central Oregon Coast Range, with the Little Luckiamute River running through its center, and was a lumber mill town incorporated in 1893.

Houses near the Willamette or creek channels deserve a flood-risk look at listing time. Rain-heavy winters also mean roofs, gutters and crawl space moisture are what buyers inspect first.

sections.h2: Which Polk County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
The Polk County Assessor sets values, and the Polk County Tax and Finance Office collects the tax. The Tax and Finance Office is at 850 Main Street, Dallas, Oregon 97338.

Value appeals go to the Property Value Appeals Board, and the county says forms are available from the County Clerk. Tax statements come from the Tax Office in late October. Four types of statement exist: real, personal, manufactured structure and utility. Each covers the tax year from July 1 to June 30, and a mortgage company that asked for the bill is noted in the statement's information section.

The county posts a lookup portal for account details, and a contact form on its tax pages. We found no phone number on the pages we reviewed, so use the form or the courthouse directory.

sections.h2: What are the key Polk County property tax dates?
sections.html:
The assessment date is January 1, tax statements go out by October 25, and the first payment is due November 15. The Assessor's calendar lists these dates and shifts them to the next business day when they land on a weekend or holiday.

DateWhat happens
January 1Valuation date for real market value
February 14Second payment due on the three-payment plan
March 15Property returns due
April 1Last day to apply for exemptions and the farm and forest deferral
April 15Senior deferral application deadline; appeals board adjourns
May 15Third payment due; unpaid real property tax becomes delinquent
October 25Last day to mail tax statements; appeal filing opens
November 15First payment due
December 31Last day to file an appeal; late exemption applications accepted with a penalty

For the 2025 to 2026 year, the Tax Office page showed payments due November 17, 2025, February 17, 2026 and May 15, 2026, after weekend adjustments. Mailed filings should carry a hand-stamped post office postmark dated on or before the due date.

sections.h2: How do Polk County payment discounts and installments work?
sections.html:
Paying the full year's tax by the November due date earns a 3% discount, and paying two-thirds earns a 2% discount on that two-thirds payment. Three equal installments carry no discount.

Payment options listed by the county include the Tax Office counter, a drop box in the courthouse parking lot, mail, online and phone. Online and phone payments carry fees. The county states that local banks no longer accept property tax payments.

At a sale, the title or escrow company usually looks up what has been paid and what is owed, then divides the current year between buyer and seller on the settlement statement. Ask them for the account status early, since a missed installment can show up as an unexpected payoff line.

sections.h2: How are Polk County assessed values capped?
sections.html:
Oregon taxes a property on its assessed value, which is the lower of real market value or maximum assessed value. Maximum assessed value can rise no more than 3% a year, apart from changes such as new construction or major remodeling, rezoning, or new lots.

Measure 5 separately limits tax by real market value, at $5 per $1,000 for education and $10 per $1,000 for general government. Voter-approved bond taxes are generally outside those limits. If a category goes over its cap, local option levies are cut first.

This is why a long-time owner's tax bill can be far lower than a bill on a similar home bought last year. It also means a lower market value does not always lower the tax, if the assessed value was already below it.

sections.h2: What happens when Polk County property taxes go unpaid?
sections.html:
Real property tax is delinquent if unpaid after May 15, and foreclosure becomes possible three years after the delinquency date. That timeline comes from the county's foreclosure page and ORS 312.010.

  • The Tax Collector prepares a foreclosure list by about July 16, and owners of record get a notice by first-class and certified mail.
  • About August 16, the list is published in the Polk County Itemizer-Observer, and the county files for judgment and adds a 5% penalty.
  • Owners may file an answer with the Circuit Court within 30 days of publication.
  • After judgment, the property is sold to the county and a two-year redemption period begins.
  • To redeem, the owner pays the delinquent taxes and interest, the 5% penalty, 9% annual interest from judgment, and a fee of at least $50. Partial payments are not accepted.

Property not redeemed passes to the county free of liens, except municipal local improvement assessments. A seller who is behind on taxes can usually clear them from sale proceeds at closing, which can end the process before it reaches judgment.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Polk County assessment?
sections.html:
File a petition with the Property Value Appeals Board by December 31, or the next business day if that date falls on a weekend or holiday. Board sessions begin the first Monday in February and may run through April 15.

Appeals focus on the real market value as of January 1. If you disagree with the board, the next step is Oregon Tax Court. A sale price, an appraisal or comparable sales near January 1 are the usual evidence, so gather them before you file.

If you are selling a Polk County house soon, an appeal rarely changes the sale. It can still be worth filing if you stay on the account for the current tax year, since the lower value would reduce what you and the buyer owe.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax in Polk County, Oregon?
faqs.a: The Polk County Tax and Finance Office, at 850 Main Street in Dallas, collects it. The Polk County Assessor sets the values.

faqs.q: When are Polk County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Payments are due November 15, February 15 and May 15, with dates moved to the next business day on weekends and holidays. Paying in full by the November date earns a 3% discount.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Polk County assessment?
faqs.a: December 31, or the next business day if it falls on a weekend or holiday. Hearings run from the first Monday in February through April 15.

faqs.q: How long can I be behind on Polk County property tax before foreclosure?
faqs.a: Foreclosure becomes possible three years after the delinquency date, and the county then gives a two-year redemption period after judgment. Taxes unpaid after May 15 are delinquent.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Polk County house with unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The unpaid tax and interest are typically paid from the sale proceeds at closing through the title company, and you should ask the Tax Office or title company for a payoff figure first.
